overview: The B-wing (A/SF-01) is a assault starfighter whose service history spans Galactic Civil War (2 BBY–5 ABY). An rotating-wing gunship designed to punch holes in Star Destroyer hulls during the Battle of Endor. Imperial archives, Rebel intelligence briefings, and Mandalorian shipyard records estimate total production at ~3,200 units, though wartime losses and black-market refits make exact counts difficult to verify.
history:
Design bureaus first drafted the B-wing (A/SF-01) during the political tensions that defined Galactic Civil War (2 BBY–5 ABY). Engineers prioritised capabilities suited to its role as a assault starfighter, balancing armour, manoeuvrability, and crew requirements against the industrial capacity of the factions that ordered it into production.

As fleet doctrine evolved, the B-wing (A/SF-01) entered front-line service in convoy escort, planetary assault, and deep-space patrol missions. An rotating-wing gunship designed to punch holes in Star Destroyer hulls during the Battle of Endor. Veterans praised its reliability under fire while analysts debated whether mass production at ~3,200 units diluted quality control across shipyard lines.

Major campaigns cemented the vessel's reputation — whether as a terror weapon, a rebel lifeline, or a smuggler's last hope. Battle damage reports show the assault starfighter could absorb punishment that would destroy lighter craft, though attrition rates climbed sharply during the bloodiest years of galactic war.

In the modern era, surviving hulls appear in private collections, museum orbits, and covert fleets. Restorers hunt spare parts across scrap worlds while historians argue the B-wing (A/SF-01) symbolises the industrial scale of conflict more than any single battle honour.
significance:
The B-wing (A/SF-01) illustrates how shipwright traditions and wartime desperation combine to shape galactic warfare. Its assault starfighter layout influenced successor designs long after production lines fell silent.

Approximately ~3,200 units hulls served during Galactic Civil War (2 BBY–5 ABY), making the class one of the most visible symbols of its faction's naval power. Colour markings and unit insignia turned anonymous factory output into icons recognised across holonet broadcasts.

For engineers and tacticians, the B-wing (A/SF-01) remains a case study in trade-offs between firepower, crew survival, and maintenance — lessons still taught at academies from Coruscant to Mandalore.
